definition: Exult means to rejoice openly and at full volume — triumphant joy let out in leaps and shouts.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word exult. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know exult should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The moment her visa approval loaded on the screen, Amara exulted — one enormous whoop that startled the whole internet cafe.
A smile is joy at its quietest — barely a ripple next to exulting.
A cheer is one burst of voiced joy; exulting is louder and longer than a cheer — whole-body celebration that refuses to sit down.

To rejoice is the plain, hymnal word for gladness — it can be quiet, inward, even solemn. To exult is rejoicing with the lid off: loud, physical, and unmistakable, triumph that leaps and shouts. A congregation can rejoice in silence; nobody exults in silence.

To crow is to exult a little too loudly and at somebody — boasting over a beaten rival with a rooster's tact. Exulting is joy aimed at the sky; crowing aims it at the loser. A team may exult all night with perfect grace and never crow once.

Exult when joy goes public — winning teams exult, rescued crews exult, grandmothers exult at spelling bees.

Then the final buzzer sounded, the scores posted, and composure went out the window.
